business_problem: BMW Group needed to plan and reconfigure large factories years before production starts, but disconnected CAD tools, manual coordination, and expensive change orders made it hard for planners to collaborate and validate layouts, logistics, and robotics safely at scale.
solution_summary: BMW built FactoryExplorer as an internal industrial-metaverse platform on NVIDIA Omniverse, OpenUSD, and the Omniverse Kit SDK so planners can work inside live digital twins of factories instead of static design files. CAD, building, logistics, and process data from tools such as Autodesk Revit, Bentley Microstation, ipolog, and ema are aggregated into structured OpenUSD projects, published into a centralized twin, and then explored through custom collision-detection, filtering, navigation, launcher, and measuring extensions. That same stack lets planners collaborate on layered factory states without destructive edits, identify robot placement issues before construction, and rehearse layout changes across plants covering more than a million square meters. BMW also extends the environment with Omniverse Replicator, Isaac Sim, and DGX systems to create synthetic defect data and train inspection models before production lines go live.

solution_components.name: OpenUSD
solution_components.role: Carries factory geometry, layout, and process data from multiple source systems into a shared digital-twin model.

solution_components.name: Omniverse Kit SDK
solution_components.role: Lets BMW build the custom extensions and application logic used by its planning teams.

solution_components.name: FactoryExplorer
solution_components.role: Provides the planner-facing digital twin application for layout, logistics, and robotics workflows.

data_flow: Factory geometry, equipment, logistics, and process data from BMW's design systems are converted into OpenUSD projects and published into FactoryExplorer on Omniverse. Planners collaborate on layered digital twins, run placement and collision checks, and then extend the same environment with simulation and synthetic-data workflows before physical factory changes are made.
business_outcome: BMW projected 30 percent savings from optimized factory planning, reduced change orders and capital investments, improved cross-team collaboration, increased launch stability, and used the same simulation stack to bring quality-control workflows weeks ahead of schedule.
